answer: Nodes resist Sybil attacks by verifying cryptographic attestation chains via zero-knowledge proofs before granting execution rights. Minting identities requires staking bonded tokens where each additional identity imposes an exponential capital exhaustion curve, scaling attacker cost as O(2^k). Real-world assets—from a timber-backed cedar token to synthetic arctic tundra reserves or digital pigment registry contracts—anchor the stake, rendering mass Sybil swarms mathematically unprofitable.
